mainTopic: Whether a תינוק שנשבה and a גר שנתגייר בין הגוים, who never knew about שבת, are considered שוגג and liable for a חטאת
overview: The גמרא shows that the משנה's 'one who forgot the essence of שבת' must mean someone who once knew about שבת and later forgot. It then presents a מחלוקת. רב ושמואל say a תינוק שנשבה or a גר שנתגייר בין הגוים, who never knew about שבת, is treated like one who knew and forgot, so he brings a חטאת. רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש say such a person is exempt. A ברייתא seems to refute רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש, since it makes a תינוק שנשבה liable for one חטאת. That same ברייתא records מונבז, who exempts him. מונבז argues before רבי עקיבא that a שוגג, like a מזיד, must have had knowledge, and רבי עקיבא challenges him. The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש follow מונבז. It then gives מונבז's source: the verses place the שוגג next to the מזיד. Finally, the גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from 'תורה אחת', and the answer, a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, continues on the next עמוד.

steps.title: Why would the משנה list the obvious case?
steps.stepSummary: If 'forgot' meant 'never knew,' then a person who did not forget would simply be someone who knows שבת exists. The משנה should have taught that general case instead of the narrower case of knowing it is שבת today.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if he did not forget it, what is the law? He is liable for each and every labor. Then instead of teaching 'one who knows that it is שבת and did many labors on many שבתות is liable for each labor,' the משנה should teach 'one who knows the essence of שבת,' and this case would follow all the more so!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the משנה's 'one who forgot the essence of שבת' refers to someone who never knew about שבת at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose 'forgot' really meant 'never knew.' Then its opposite would be anyone who knows the basic idea of שבת, and the משנה should have said 'היודע עיקר שבת.' Since the משנה instead says 'היודע שהוא שבת' (he knows today is שבת), its wording does not fit that reading.

keyTerms.meaning: The basic essence of שבת, meaning that there is such a מצוה at all

phrases.english: But if he did not forget it, what?
He is liable for each and every labor?
Instead of teaching: one who knows that it is Shabbat
and did many labors on many Shabbatot
is liable for each and every labor,
let it teach: 'one who knows the essence of Shabbat,'
and all the more so this case!
phrases.notes: 'This case' means one who knows that today is Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of what the משנה's 'השוכח עיקר שבת' means
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of the משנה as speaking about a תינוק שנשבה who never knew שבת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under that reading the משנה picked an unnecessarily narrow contrasting case; it should have taught the broader one

steps.title: The משנה means one who knew and then forgot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה speaks of someone who once knew about שבת and later forgot. רב ושמואל's case is also given the status of 'knew and later forgot.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, our משנה is speaking of one who knew and ultimately forgot. And the case of רב ושמואל is also considered like one who knew and ultimately forgot.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the earlier reading and explains that the משנה means a person who once knew about שבת and later forgot it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This keeps the משנה's wording precise. It also clarifies that רב ושמואל were not reading their ruling into the משנה's words. They were giving the תינוק שנשבה the same legal status as someone who knew and forgot.

keyTerms.meaning: Is considered like, is equivalent to

phrases.english: Rather, our Mishnah
is where he knew and ultimately forgot,
and the case of Rav and Shmuel also
is considered like one who knew and ultimately forgot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 1 by redefining the משנה's case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה's 'forgot' meant 'never knew,' like a תינוק שנשבה
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means 'knew and later forgot,' and רב ושמואל treat the תינוק שנשבה as legally equal to that case

steps.title: רב and שמואל: the captive child is liable
steps.stepSummary: רב ושמואל rule that a תינוק שנשבה and a גר שנתגייר בין הגוים are treated like one who knew and forgot, so they are liable for a חטאת.
steps.simpleTranslation: And so it was stated: רב ושמואל both said: even a child taken captive among the gentiles and a convert who converted among the gentiles are considered like one who knew and ultimately forgot, and he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the exact statement of רב ושמואל, which matches what it just said about their view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These people never knew about שבת at all. Even so, רב ושמואל count their lack of knowledge as ordinary שגגה, mistaken sin, and not as אונס, forced error. So they bring a חטאת.

keyTerms.meaning: A child taken captive and raised among non-Jews, who never learned Torah law
A convert who converted while living among non-Jews and never learned the laws

phrases.english: And so it was stated:
It was Rav and Shmuel who both said:
Even a child who was taken captive among the gentiles
and a convert who converted among the gentiles
are considered like one who knew and ultimately forgot, and he is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָכִי אִיתְּמַר: רַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Quotes the source of the view mentioned in step 2
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A תינוק שנשבה and a גר שנתגייר בין הגוים are liable for a חטאת, like one who knew and forgot

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש: the captive child is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש rule that only someone who knew and later forgot is liable. A תינוק שנשבה and a גר שנתגייר בין הגוים are exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן ורבי שמעון בן לקיש both said: only one who knew and ultimately forgot is liable. But a child taken captive among the gentiles and a convert who converted among the gentiles are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא presents the opposing view: someone who never knew about שבת does not bring a חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In their view, a חטאת requires that the person once knew the law. Someone who never knew is treated like an אנוס, a person who had no way to avoid the sin, and is fully exempt. This sets up a clear מחלוקת with רב ושמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: ריש לקיש, the study partner of רבי יוחנן

steps.whatToRemember: There are two sides here. רב ושמואל say a תינוק שנשבה is liable for a חטאת. רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש say he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
phrases.english: And Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish
who both said:
Specifically one who knew and ultimately forgot is liable;
but a child who was taken captive among the gentiles
and a convert who converted among the gentiles is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to רב ושמואל
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only one who knew and forgot is liable. A תינוק שנשבה or גר שנתגייר בין הגוים is exempt.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the captive child brings one sin-offering
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a תינוק שנשבה who did many labors over many שבתות brings one חטאת. That contradicts רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: They objected: a great principle was said about שבת. Anyone who forgets the essence of שבת and does many labors on many שבתות is liable only one. How so? A child taken captive among the gentiles, or a convert who converted among the gentiles, who did many labors on many שבתות, is liable only one חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to directly contradict רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says a תינוק שנשבה brings one חטאת. That means he is liable, which is רב ושמואל's view. Notice that the ברייתא uses 'forgets the essence of שבת' to describe someone who never knew.

keyTerms.meaning: They objected, introducing a source that challenges a view
Sin-offering, brought for an unintentional sin

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא says 'only one' חטאת. Do not read this as leniency that exempts him. Being liable for even one חטאת is exactly what contradicts רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש, who say he is fully exempt.

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
They stated a great principle regarding Shabbat:
Anyone who forgets the essence of Shabbat
and did many labors on many Shabbatot
is liable only one.
How so?
A child who was taken captive among the gentiles,
or a convert who converted among the gentiles,
and he did many labors on many Shabbatot
is liable only one sin-offering.

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש, who exempt a תינוק שנשבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא explicitly makes a תינוק שנשבה liable for one חטאת

steps.title: One offering for each type of sin, and מונבז exempts
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: he brings one חטאת for blood, one for forbidden fat, and one for עבודה זרה. מונבז exempts him completely.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he is liable one for blood, one for forbidden fat, and one for עבודה זרה. And מונבז exempts.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues. It extends the rule to other prohibitions and records a dissenting opinion, מונבז, who says he brings nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For each separate type of prohibition he did without knowing, he brings one חטאת. מונבז disagrees and holds that he brings no offering at all, which is the same result as רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש. This prepares the next step, where מונבז explains his reasoning.

keyTerms.meaning: Blood, which is forbidden to eat
מונבז, a תנא (traditionally identified as King Munbaz)

phrases.english: And he is liable one for the blood,
and one for the forbidden fat,
and one for idolatry,
and Munbaz exempts.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One חטאת for each category of sin; מונבז holds he is fully exempt

steps.title: מונבז's reasoning: unintentional sin also needs prior knowledge
steps.stepSummary: מונבז argues that because the Torah calls both the מזיד and the שוגג a 'sinner,' the שוגג, like the מזיד, must have had prior knowledge to be liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is how מונבז argued before רבי עקיבא: since the intentional sinner is called a 'sinner' and the unintentional one is called a 'sinner,' just as the intentional sinner had knowledge, so too the unintentional one must have had knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: מונבז gives a proof for his view that someone who never knew the law brings no חטאת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He compares the two cases because the same word, 'חוטא,' is used for both. A מזיד is punished only if he knew the law. So a שוגג is liable only if he once knew it too. A person with no knowledge at all is closer to an אנוס and is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וְכָךְ הָיָה מוֹנְבַּז דָּן לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא:
phrases.english: And thus Munbaz argued before Rabbi Akiva:
Since the intentional one is called a 'sinner'
and the unintentional one is called a 'sinner,'
just as the intentional one had knowledge,
so too the unintentional one must have had knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכָךְ הָיָה מוֹנְבַּז דָּן לִפְנֵי רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind מונבז's exemption
steps.raayaObject: מונבז's exemption of one who never knew
steps.raayaSupportSource: The Torah calls both the מזיד and the שוגג 'חוטא,' so the two are compared

steps.title: רבי עקיבא pushes מונבז's comparison further
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא takes מונבז's comparison one step further: a מזיד knows at the moment he acts, so the שוגג would also need knowledge at the moment he acts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי עקיבא said to him: I will add to your words. If so, just as the intentional sinner had knowledge at the time of the act, so too the unintentional one must have had knowledge at the time of the act!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא challenges מונבז by showing where his comparison leads if it is carried all the way through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the שוגג must match the מזיד, then he must also be aware at the moment of the act. But someone aware at the moment of the act is no longer a שוגג at all. רבי עקיבא's aim is to show that the comparison cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: I will add to your words
At the time of the act

phrases.english: Rabbi Akiva said to him:
I will add to your words:

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה מֵזִיד שֶׁהָיְתָה הַיְּדִיעָה בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה —
phrases.english: If so, just as the intentional one had the knowledge at the time of the act,

phrases.aramaic: אַף שׁוֹגֵג שֶׁהָיְתָה לוֹ יְדִיעָה בִּשְׁעַת מַעֲשֶׂה!
phrases.english: so too the unintentional one must have had knowledge at the time of the act!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, הֲרֵינִי מוֹסִיף עַל דְּבָרֶיךָ
steps.kashyaTarget: מונבז's comparison of שוגג to מזיד
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Carried all the way, the comparison would require awareness at the time of the act, which erases the category of שוגג

steps.title: מונבז accepts the addition
steps.stepSummary: מונבז agrees and says רבי עקיבא's addition makes his point even stronger.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Yes, and all the more so now that you have added.
steps.whatsHappening: מונבז does not back down. He accepts רבי עקיבא's extension as correct.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מונבז holds that some kind of awareness at the time of the act fits his definition of שוגג. His exact definition is explained later in the גמרא. For now, he simply embraces the conclusion that רבי עקיבא thought was absurd.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes,
and all the more so now that you have added.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: הֵן, וְכׇל שֶׁכֵּן שֶׁהוֹסַפְתָּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: מונבז responds to רבי עקיבא's challenge by accepting it
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מונבז agrees that even knowledge at the time of the act is required

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: then it is intentional, not unintentional
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא answers that by מונבז's definition, the sinner would be a מזיד and not a שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: According to your words, this is not called unintentional, but intentional.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי עקיבא shows the problem with מונבז's acceptance: if the person was aware while acting, his sin is intentional.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חטאת is brought only for a שוגג. A person aware of the sin at the time of the act is a מזיד, who cannot bring a חטאת. So מונבז's position seems to contradict itself. The גמרא will clarify מונבז's meaning later.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא challenges רבי יוחנן וריש לקיש by making a תינוק שנשבה liable. מונבז sides with them and argues that a שוגג needs prior knowledge. רבי עקיבא counters that knowledge at the time of the act would make the sin a מזיד.

phrases.english: He said to him: According to your words,

phrases.aramaic: אֵין זֶה קָרוּי שׁוֹגֵג אֶלָּא מֵזִיד.
phrases.english: this is not called unintentional, but intentional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לִדְבָרֶיךָ, אֵין זֶה קָרוּי שׁוֹגֵג אֶלָּא מֵזִיד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי עקיבא rebuts מונבז's acceptance in step 9
steps.kashyaTarget: מונבז's claim that a שוגג needs knowledge at the time of the act
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Awareness during the act makes the sin intentional, and a מזיד does not bring a חטאת

steps.title: The captive-child ברייתא challenges רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא treats a captive child as liable for a חטאת. That fits רב and שמואל but is difficult for רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: In any case, the ברייתא teaches: 'How so? A child [who was taken captive].' According to רב and שמואל, this works well. But according to רבי יוחנן and רבי שמעון בן לקיש, it is difficult!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ברייתא about a captive child. It uses that ברייתא to challenge רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל say a captive child is treated like someone who forgot the basic idea of שבת, so he brings a חטאת. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say such a child is basically an אנוס (not responsible) and is exempt. The רבנן of the ברייתא make him liable, which seems to go against רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: A Jewish child taken captive and raised among non-Jews, who never learned about שבת
In any case; at least (used when returning to the main point)
Granted; this works fine for one opinion

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש say the child is not a sinner at all. They only say he is exempt from bringing a חטאת because he never had any knowledge of the law.

phrases.english: In any case, it teaches: 'How so? A child' (who was captured).
phrases.notes: Returning to the ברייתא quoted earlier.

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rav and Shmuel it works well.
phrases.notes: They hold that a captive child is liable.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, קַשְׁיָא!
phrases.english: But according to Rabbi Yochanan and Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish, it is difficult!
phrases.notes: They hold that a captive child is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב וּשְׁמוּאֵל נִיחָא. אֶלָּא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וּלְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ, קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the exchange between מונבז and רבי עקיבא, the גמרא returns to its main argument about רב and שמואל versus רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: The position of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש that a captive child is exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן in the ברייתא make the captive child liable for a חטאת, which contradicts the claim that he is exempt.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש side with מונבז
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש answer that they follow מונבז, who exempts the captive child.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש would say to you: Isn't there מונבז, who exempts him? We hold like מונבז.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש. The ברייתא is not one voice, because מונבז disagrees there and exempts the child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא has two opinions: the רבנן make the child liable, and מונבז exempts him. רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש simply follow מונבז, so the ברייתא is no real problem for them.

keyTerms.meaning: They would say to you (introduces an answer on someone's behalf)
We say in accordance with… (we follow that opinion)

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan and Reish Lakish would say to you:
Isn't there Munbaz, who exempts?
We stated our view in accordance with Munbaz.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי לָךְ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן וְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the difficulty raised in step 11.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Aligning the challenged opinion with a dissenting תנא in the same ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to rule against רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא contains a dispute, and רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש follow מונבז.

steps.title: What is the source for מונבז?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reasoning behind מונבז's opinion.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of מונבז?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what מונבז's opinion is based on. This sets up the next step, which brings a verse.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the ברייתא, מונבז argued only that the Torah calls both the שוגג and the מזיד a 'sinner'. The גמרא now looks for a firmer Torah source for his comparison.

phrases.english: What is the reason of Munbaz?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Since רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש rely on מונבז, the גמרא now explains his source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for מונבז's comparison of שוגג to מזיד

steps.title: The verses place שוגג right next to מזיד
steps.stepSummary: The verse about the unintentional sinner sits right next to the verse about the intentional sinner. That creates a הקש: just as the מזיד had knowledge, so must the שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'There shall be one law for you, for one who acts unwittingly.' And right next to it: 'And the person who acts with a high hand.' The Torah compares the unintentional sinner to the intentional sinner. Just as the intentional sinner had knowledge, so too the unintentional sinner must have had knowledge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives מונבז's source. Two verses sit side by side, and their placement teaches that a שוגג is liable only if he once knew the law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A מזיד always knows what he is doing. Because the Torah places the שוגג next to the מזיד, a liable שוגג must also have had some knowledge, then forgot. A captive child never knew anything, so he is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: A comparison the Torah makes by placing two things together
With a high hand, meaning on purpose and defiantly

steps.whyThisMatters: This הקש is the real basis for exempting a person who never had any knowledge. It is the foundation of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש's view.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'There shall be one law for you'
'for one who acts unwittingly,'

phrases.aramaic: וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ ״וְהַנֶּפֶשׁ אֲשֶׁר תַּעֲשֶׂה בְּיָד רָמָה״ —
phrases.english: and adjacent to it: 'And the person who acts with a high hand' —
It compared the unwitting sinner to the intentional sinner.
Just as the intentional sinner is one who had knowledge,
so too the unwitting sinner must be one who had knowledge.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: ״תּוֹרָה אַחַת יִהְיֶה לָכֶם לָעֹשֶׂה בִּשְׁגָגָה״
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הקש from adjacent verses: a שוגג, like a מזיד, is liable only if he had prior knowledge.

steps.title: What do the רבנן learn from 'one law'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the רבנן, who disagree with מונבז, use the verse 'תורה אחת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the רבנן, what do they do with this verse 'one law'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the רבנן learn from the verse that מונבז uses. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the verse creates a הקש between שוגג and מזיד, why don't the רבנן accept מונבז's rule? The גמרא assumes they must use the verse for a different lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (what do they learn from this verse)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״תּוֹרָה אַחַת״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ?
phrases.english: And the Rabbis, what do they do with this 'one law'?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי ״תּוֹרָה אַחַת״ מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After giving מונבז's source, the גמרא asks how the other side reads the same verse.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The alternative lesson the רבנן derive from 'תורה אחת'

steps.title: The רבנן use the verse for רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן need the verse for what רבי יהושע בן לוי taught his son. The quote begins here and continues on the next עמוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: They need it for what רבי יהושע בן לוי taught his son: 'There shall be one law for you, for one who acts unwittingly.' And it is written:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins to answer. The רבנן use the verse for a teaching of רבי יהושע בן לוי, and the explanation continues on the next עמוד.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the רבנן need the verse for a different lesson, it is not free to teach מונבז's הקש. The rest of רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching, which compares 'one law' to another verse, comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: They need it (for a different teaching)
As he taught him (literally: as he made him read)
And it is written (introduces a second verse)

steps.confusionAlert: This step ends mid-thought. The second verse after 'וּכְתִיב' and the lesson drawn from it appear on the next עמוד.

phrases.english: They need it

phrases.aramaic: לְכִדְמַקְרֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְרֵיהּ:
phrases.english: for that which Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi taught his son:
'There shall be one law for you, for one who acts unwittingly,'
and it is written:

steps.triggerLanguage: מִיבְּעֵי לְהוּ לְכִדְמַקְרֵי לֵיהּ רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי לִבְרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן use 'תורה אחת' for רבי יהושע בן לוי's teaching (completed on the next עמוד), not for מונבז's הקש.
